claim: The actin cytoskeleton plays important roles in the formation and internalization of endocytic vesicles.
source: The actin cytoskeleton plays important roles in the formation and internalization of endocytic vesicles.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations to prior work in the introduction.

claim: In yeast, endocytic vesicles move towards early endosomes along actin cables.
source: In yeast, endocytic vesicles move towards early endosomes along actin cables, however, the molecular machinery regulating interaction between endocytic vesicles and actin cables is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction (Huckaba et al., 2004; Toshima et al., 2006).

claim: The Eps15-like protein Pan1p plays a key role in actin-mediated endocytosis.
source: The Eps15-like protein Pan1p plays a key role in actin-mediated endocytosis and is negatively regulated by Ark1 and Prk1 kinases.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: Pan1p is negatively regulated by Ark1 and Prk1 kinases.
source: The Eps15-like protein Pan1p plays a key role in actin-mediated endocytosis and is negatively regulated by Ark1 and Prk1 kinases.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: pan1-18TA mutant displayed almost the same endocytic defect as ark1Δ prk1Δ cells.
source: Here we show that pan1 mutated to prevent phosphorylation at all 18 threonines, pan1-18TA, displayed almost the same endocytic defect as ark1Δ prk1Δ cells, and contained abnormal actin concentrations including several endocytic compartments.
evidence: This is supported by the α-factor internalization assay data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: pan1-18TA mutant contained abnormal actin concentrations including several endocytic compartments.
source: Here we show that pan1 mutated to prevent phosphorylation at all 18 threonines, pan1-18TA, displayed almost the same endocytic defect as ark1Δ prk1Δ cells, and contained abnormal actin concentrations including several endocytic compartments.
evidence: This is supported by phalloidin staining in Figure 1D and localization data in Figure 2.

claim: Early endosomes were highly localized in the actin concentrations in pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Early endosomes were highly localized in the actin concentrations and displayed movement along actin cables.
evidence: This is supported by the localization data in Figure 2 showing Hse1p, Mvb12p, and Vps36p colocalization with actin clumps.

claim: Early endosomes displayed movement along actin cables in pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Early endosomes were highly localized in the actin concentrations and displayed movement along actin cables.
evidence: This is supported by the live-cell imaging data described in the Results section.

claim: The dephosphorylated form of Pan1p caused stable associations between endocytic vesicles and actin cables.
source: The dephosphorylated form of Pan1p also caused stable associations between endocytic vesicles and actin cables, and between endocytic vesicles and endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 4 showing Pan1-18TA-mCherry-labeled vesicles stably associating with actin cables.

claim: The dephosphorylated form of Pan1p caused stable associations between endocytic vesicles and endosomes.
source: The dephosphorylated form of Pan1p also caused stable associations between endocytic vesicles and actin cables, and between endocytic vesicles and endosomes.
evidence: This is supported by the data in Figure 4F,G showing colocalization of Pan1-18TA-mCherry with Hse1p-labeled endosomes.

claim: Pan1 phosphorylation is part of a novel mechanism that regulates endocytic compartment interactions with each other and with actin cables.
source: Thus Pan1 phosphorylation is part of a novel mechanism that regulates endocytic compartment interactions with each other and with actin cables.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Transient actin polymerization at the endocytic site is required for the formation and internalization of a CCV.
source: In the early stages of the endocytic pathway, transient actin polymerization at the endocytic site is required for the formation and internalization of a CCV (Kaksonen et al., 2003; Merrifield et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Pan1p has a lower NPF activity compared to Las17p and Myo3/5p.
source: Compared to Las17p and Myo3/5p, Pan1p has a lower NPF activity, and mutation in the Arp2/3 complex binding region of Pan1p causes only a minor defect in actin polymerization at endocytic sites because of the functional redundancy with Las17p (Sun et al., 2006; Toshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Pan1-15TA directly binds to F-actin with high affinity.
source: However, a form of Pan1p mutated to prevent phosphorylation at 15 threonines, Pan1-15TA, directly binds to F-actin with high affinity and its expression causes abnormal cytoplasmic actin concentrations, also called actin clumps (Toshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Expression of Pan1-15TA causes abnormal cytoplasmic actin concentrations.
source: However, a form of Pan1p mutated to prevent phosphorylation at 15 threonines, Pan1-15TA, directly binds to F-actin with high affinity and its expression causes abnormal cytoplasmic actin concentrations, also called actin clumps (Toshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Ark1p and Prk1p are recruited to endocytic sites 1–2 s after commencement of actin assembly and CCV internalization.
source: In budding yeast, Ark1p and Prk1p are recruited to endocytic sites 1–2 s after commencement of actin assembly and CCV internalization, and phosphorylate several endocytic proteins, including Sla1p, Ent1/2p, Yap1801/2p, Scd5p, and Pan1p, to disassemble endocytic coat proteins and actin (Cope et al., 1999; Henry et al., 2003; Toret et al., 2008; Watson et al., 2001; Zeng and Cai, 1999; Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ark1p and Prk1p phosphorylate several endocytic proteins including Sla1p, Ent1/2p, Yap1801/2p, Scd5p, and Pan1p.
source: In budding yeast, Ark1p and Prk1p are recruited to endocytic sites 1–2 s after commencement of actin assembly and CCV internalization, and phosphorylate several endocytic proteins, including Sla1p, Ent1/2p, Yap1801/2p, Scd5p, and Pan1p, to disassemble endocytic coat proteins and actin (Cope et al., 1999; Henry et al., 2003; Toret et al., 2008; Watson et al., 2001; Zeng and Cai, 1999; Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Phosphorylation of Pan1p by Ark1/Prk1 kinases is believed to be important for disassembly of the Pan1p complex.
source: Pan1p is one of the key targets of Ark1/Prk1 kinases, and phosphorylation of Pan1p by Ark1/Prk1 kinases is believed to be important for disassembly of the Pan1p complex, composed of several endocytic proteins (Toshima et al., 2005; Wendland and Emr, 1998; Zeng and Cai, 1999; Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Disruption of the normal phosphorylation cycle by deletion or chemical inhibition of Ark1/Prk1 kinases leads to the concentration of actin in association with endocytic vesicles.
source: Interestingly, disruption of the normal phosphorylation cycle by deletion or chemical inhibition of Ark1/Prk1 kinases leads to the concentration of actin in association with endocytic vesicles (Sekiya-Kawasaki et al., 2003; Toshima et al., 2005), suggesting a role for Pan1p and other substrates in regulating interaction between endocytic vesicles and the actin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Endocytic vesicles move away from the plasma membrane in an association with actin cables.
source: After being internalized, endocytic vesicles move away from the plasma membrane in an association with actin cables that is still mechanistically unexplained (Huckaba et al., 2004; Toshima et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Actin cables are bundles of actin filaments that align along the long axis of budding yeast.
source: Yeast actin cables, which are bundles of actin filaments that align along the long axis of budding yeast, are crucial for the establishment of cell polarity (Yang and Pon, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Actin cables are crucial for the establishment of cell polarity.
source: Yeast actin cables, which are bundles of actin filaments that align along the long axis of budding yeast, are crucial for the establishment of cell polarity (Yang and Pon, 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Type V myosins Myo2/4p mediate the movement of cargo from the minus to plus ends of actin filaments.
source: Many of these types of transport along actin cables are known to depend on the type V myosins, Myo2/4p, which mediate the movement of cargo from the minus to plus ends of actin filaments (Bretscher, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Transport of endocytic vesicles along actin cables is not likely to depend on Myo2/4p myosins.
source: However, transport of endocytic vesicles along actin cables is not likely to depend on these myosins, because a temperature sensitive mutant of MYO2 (myo2-66) or a deletion of MYO4 gene did not exhibit any defect in endocytosis (Govindan et al., 1995; Haarer et al., 1994).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Endocytic vesicle movement occurs at the same velocity and in the same direction as the movement of actin cables.
source: Interestingly, a previous study demonstrated that endocytic vesicle movement occurs at the same velocity and in the same direction as the movement of actin cables (Huckaba et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: An endocytic vesicle stays at the same position on the cable and moves together with the actin cable.
source: They also reported that an endocytic vesicle stays at the same position on the cable and moves together with the actin cable, suggesting that endocytic vesicles are fixed on the actin cables and move as a result of actin cable flow (Huckaba et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Early endosomes associate with the actin cytoskeleton.
source: In addition to endocytic vesicles, early endosomes also associate with the actin cytoskeleton, and the motility of endosomes is significantly inhibited by treatment of latrunculin A (LatA), a drug that sequesters actin monomers (Chang et al., 2003; Fernandez-Borja et al., 2005; Toshima et al., 2006; Voigt et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The motility of endosomes is significantly inhibited by treatment of latrunculin A (LatA).
source: In addition to endocytic vesicles, early endosomes also associate with the actin cytoskeleton, and the motility of endosomes is significantly inhibited by treatment of latrunculin A (LatA), a drug that sequesters actin monomers (Chang et al., 2003; Fernandez-Borja et al., 2005; Toshima et al., 2006; Voigt et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and data in Figure 3C,D.

claim: Early endosome motility does not depend on Myo2/4p.
source: Similarly to endocytic vesicles, early endosome motility also does not depend on Myo2/4p (Toshima et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Pan1p contains three additional Ark1p/Prk1p consensus sequences (MQPNIT464G, MMPQTT480G, and MMPQTT487G) all located in the second LR region.
source: Pan1p contains three more such Ark1p/Prk1p consensus sequences (MQPNIT464G, MMPQTT480G, and MMPQTT487G) all located in the second LR region (Figure 1A) (Huang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: pan1-18TA mutant showed a more severe growth retardation phenotype than pan1-15TA.
source: When we additionally mutated these sites to create pan1-18TA, we observed a more severe growth retardation phenotype than in pan1-15TA (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Pan1-18TA protein was expressed normally.
source: The Pan1-18TA protein was expressed normally, but its phosphorylation was mostly inhibited (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Pan1-18TA phosphorylation was mostly inhibited.
source: The Pan1-18TA protein was expressed normally, but its phosphorylation was mostly inhibited (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: pan1-18TA mutant cells displayed prominent actin concentrations.
source: pan1-18TA mutant cells displayed prominent actin concentrations and a more severe defect in endocytic internalization (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: pan1-18TA mutant cells displayed a more severe defect in endocytic internalization.
source: pan1-18TA mutant cells displayed prominent actin concentrations and a more severe defect in endocytic internalization (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: 95% of Pan1-18TA-GFP colocalized with actin clumps or smaller, peripheral actin patches.
source: Pan1-18TA-GFP also showed defects in localization, with 95% colocalizing with actin clumps or smaller, peripheral actin patches, similar to Pan1-15TA (Figure 1F) (Toshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In wild-type cells, Pan1p is recruited to cortical patches early, arriving ~20 s before actin is detected.
source: This is in contrast to wild-type cells, in which Pan1p is recruited to cortical patches early, arriving ~20 s before actin is detected, and associates with actin for ~10–15 s (Kaksonen, 2003), resulting in ~30% of Pan1p colocalizing with Abp1p (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In wild-type cells, Pan1p associates with actin for ~10–15 s.
source: This is in contrast to wild-type cells, in which Pan1p is recruited to cortical patches early, arriving ~20 s before actin is detected, and associates with actin for ~10–15 s (Kaksonen, 2003), resulting in ~30% of Pan1p colocalizing with Abp1p (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: In wild-type cells, ~30% of Pan1p colocalizes with Abp1p.
source: This is in contrast to wild-type cells, in which Pan1p is recruited to cortical patches early, arriving ~20 s before actin is detected, and associates with actin for ~10–15 s (Kaksonen, 2003), resulting in ~30% of Pan1p colocalizing with Abp1p (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Internalized A594-α-factor moved to actin clumps in pan1-18TA before being transported to the vacuole.
source: Interestingly, internalized A594-α-factor moved to actin clumps in pan1-18TA before being transported to the vacuole, while the actin remained in clumps (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: The endocytic cargo can transit through the actin clumps before arriving at the vacuole.
source: This result suggests that the endocytic cargo can transit through the actin clumps before arriving at the vacuole.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the A594-α-factor tracking data in Figure 1G.

claim: Sla1p contains 10 potential Prk1 phosphorylation sites.
source: Sla1p contains the most potential Prk1 phosphorylation sites among these proteins (Zeng et al., 2001).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The Sla1-10TA mutant was expressed at similar levels to the wild-type protein.
source: We first confirmed that the Sla1-10TA mutant was expressed at similar levels to the wild-type protein, and that its phosphorylation was severely inhibited (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Sla1-10TA phosphorylation was severely inhibited.
source: We first confirmed that the Sla1-10TA mutant was expressed at similar levels to the wild-type protein, and that its phosphorylation was severely inhibited (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The sla1-10TA mutant exhibited almost the same growth as wild-type cells.
source: While cells lacking the SLA1 gene were temperature-sensitive for growth at 37°C, the sla1-10TA mutant exhibited almost the same growth as wild-type cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: F-actin staining in fixed sla1-10TA mutants closely resembled that of wild-type cells.
source: Alexa Fluor 488-phalloidin staining of F-actin in fixed sla1-10TA mutants closely resembled that of wild-type cells, with brightly stained actin patches and weakly stained actin cables (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: In sla1-10TA mutants, Sla1p and Abp1p patches formed and disappeared with typical inward movement.
source: In the sla1-10TA mutants, Sla1p and Abp1p patches formed and disappeared with the typical inward movement, and their lifetimes were slightly prolonged to 43 ± 11 s and 15 ± 3 s, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F.

claim: In sla1-10TA mutants, Sla1p and Abp1p lifetimes were slightly prolonged to 43 ± 11 s and 15 ± 3 s, respectively.
source: In the sla1-10TA mutants, Sla1p and Abp1p patches formed and disappeared with the typical inward movement, and their lifetimes were slightly prolonged to 43 ± 11 s and 15 ± 3 s, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Endocytic internalization was only slightly affected in sla1-10TA mutants.
source: We also examined the effect of sla1-10TA mutants on endocytic internalization by assessing the ingression of 35S-labeled α-factor, and found that it was only slightly affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The pan1-18TA sla1-10TA double mutant exhibited only a negligible additive effect, when compared to the pan1-18TA single mutant.
source: Furthermore, the pan1-18TA sla1-10TA double mutant exhibited only a negligible additive effect, when compared to the pan1-18TA single mutant (Figure 1E, and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,H).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D,H.

claim: Pan1p is the major in vivo substrate of Ark1/Prk1 kinases during their regulation of endocytosis.
source: These findings indicate that Pan1p is the major in vivosubstrate of Ark1/Prk1 kinases during their regulation of endocytosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of pan1-18TA and sla1-10TA mutant phenotypes.

claim: Among 14 endosomal proteins examined, Hse1p, Mvb12p, and Vps36p showed a clear change in localization to actin clumps in the pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Among the 14 proteins examined, three – Hse1p, Mvb12p, and Vps36p – showed a clear change in localization to Abp1-mCherry-labeled actin clumps in the pan1-18TA mutant (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Hse1p, Mvb12p, and Vps36p were contained in 60–65% of the actin clumps in pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Hse1p, Mvb12p, and Vps36p, which function at an early stage of the ESCRT pathway on the way to the MVB, were contained in 60–65% of the actin clumps, whereas Vps24p and Vps4p, which function at a later stage of the ESCRT pathway, were contained in 25–30% of the actin clumps (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Vps24p and Vps4p were contained in 25–30% of the actin clumps in pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Hse1p, Mvb12p, and Vps36p, which function at an early stage of the ESCRT pathway on the way to the MVB, were contained in 60–65% of the actin clumps, whereas Vps24p and Vps4p, which function at a later stage of the ESCRT pathway, were contained in 25–30% of the actin clumps (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Earlier stage endosomes are highly localized to actin clumps in pan1-18TA mutant cells.
source: These results indicate that earlier stage endosomes are highly localized to actin clumps in pan1-18TA mutant cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential localization of early vs. late endosomal markers to actin clumps.

claim: Hse1-3GFP was clearly detected as numerous small puncta throughout the cytoplasm and prevacuolar compartments (PVCs).
source: Hse1-3GFP was clearly detected as numerous small puncta throughout the cytoplasm and prevacuolar compartments (PVCs) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Hse1p exhibited high colocalization with Mvb12p.
source: By comparing the localization of Hse1-mCherry with GFP-tagged markers, we found that Hse1p exhibited high colocalization with Mvb12p, partial colocalization with Ear1p and Vps26p, and little colocalization with Sec7p (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Hse1p exhibited partial colocalization with Ear1p and Vps26p.
source: By comparing the localization of Hse1-mCherry with GFP-tagged markers, we found that Hse1p exhibited high colocalization with Mvb12p, partial colocalization with Ear1p and Vps26p, and little colocalization with Sec7p (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Hse1p exhibited little colocalization with Sec7p.
source: By comparing the localization of Hse1-mCherry with GFP-tagged markers, we found that Hse1p exhibited high colocalization with Mvb12p, partial colocalization with Ear1p and Vps26p, and little colocalization with Sec7p (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: Hse1-3GFP was highly colocalized with A594-α-factor-labeled endosomes at 5–10 min after α-factor internalization.
source: Hse1-3GFP was highly colocalized with A594-α-factor-labeled endosomes at 5–10 min after α-factor internalization, whereas Vps26-GFP was mainly colocalized with A594-α-factor-labeled endosomes at 10 min (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E,G.

claim: Vps26-GFP was mainly colocalized with A594-α-factor-labeled endosomes at 10 min after α-factor internalization.
source: Hse1-3GFP was highly colocalized with A594-α-factor-labeled endosomes at 5–10 min after α-factor internalization, whereas Vps26-GFP was mainly colocalized with A594-α-factor-labeled endosomes at 10 min (Figure 3—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F,G.

claim: Hse1p is widely localized from early to late endosomes.
source: These data indicate that Hse1p is widely localized from early to late endosomes and partially colocalized with Vps26p at late endosomes both in wild-type and pan1-18TA cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the colocalization data with various markers.

claim: Hse1p is partially colocalized with Vps26p at late endosomes both in wild-type and pan1-18TA cells.
source: These data indicate that Hse1p is widely localized from early to late endosomes and partially colocalized with Vps26p at late endosomes both in wild-type and pan1-18TA cells.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,H.

claim: Vps21p exhibited lower localization at the actin clumps (~33%), compared to Hse1p.
source: Unexpectedly, Vps21p, yeast Rab5, which is known to be localized at early-to-late endosomes (Cabrera et al., 2013; Puchner et al., 2013; Toshima et al., 2014), exhibited lower localization at the actin clumps (~33%), compared to Hse1p (Figure 2A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2A,B.

claim: Hse1p colocalizes with A594-α-factor slightly more than Vps21p at 10 min after α-factor internalization.
source: Consistent with a recent study by Arlt et al. reporting that an ESCRT-I subunit, Vps23, is recruited to endosomes earlier than Vps21p (Arlt et al., 2015), we found that Hse1p colocalizes with A594-α-factor slightly more than Vps21p at 10 min after α-factor internalization (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Endosomes at the early stage of endocytosis are highly localized to actin clumps.
source: These results, therefore, suggest that endosomes at the early stage of endocytosis are highly localized to actin clumps.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential timing of Hse1p vs. Vps21p recruitment to endosomes.

claim: Early-stage endosomes moved with an average speed of 125 ± 119 nm/s in wild-type cells.
source: Quantification of endosome velocity revealed that early-stage endosomes moved with an average speed of 125 ± 119 nm/s (n = 100), whereas late-stage endosomes moved with an average speed of 156 ± 130 nm/s (n = 100) in wild-type cells (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Late-stage endosomes moved with an average speed of 156 ± 130 nm/s in wild-type cells.
source: Quantification of endosome velocity revealed that early-stage endosomes moved with an average speed of 125 ± 119 nm/s (n = 100), whereas late-stage endosomes moved with an average speed of 156 ± 130 nm/s (n = 100) in wild-type cells (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: LatA treatment led to a significant decrease in the velocity of early-stage endosomes (~23 ± 47 nm/s).
source: Concomitantly, LatA treatment led to a significant decrease in the velocity of early-stage endosomes (~23 ± 47 nm/s) (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: The velocity of late-stage endosomes was not significantly affected by LatA treatment (~119 ± 112 nm/s).
source: In contrast, the velocity of late-stage endosomes was not significantly affected by LatA treatment (~119 ± 112 nm/s) (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: Hse1p-labeled endosomes localized along, and moved on, actin cables.
source: Simultaneous imaging revealed that Hse1p-labeled endosomes localized along, and moved on, actin cables (Figure 3E,F, and Video 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3E,F and Video 1.

claim: SMIFH2 treatment led to actin cable disassembly, followed by a decrease in the velocity of endosomes (~60 ± 53 nm/s).
source: As expected, SMIFH2 treatment led to actin cable disassembly, followed by a decrease in the velocity of endosomes (~60 ± 53 nm/s).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3G,H.

claim: CK-666 inhibited vesicle internalization, but endosome motilities were little affected (~126 ± 123 nm/s).
source: In contrast, CK-666 inhibited vesicle internalization, but endosome motilities were little affected (~126 ± 123 nm/s) (Figure 3G,H, and Video 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3G,H and Video 2.

claim: The movement of early-stage endosomes is dependent on formin-dependent actin polymerization.
source: These results indicate that the movement of early-stage endosomes is dependent on formin-dependent actin polymerization.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential effects of SMIFH2 vs. CK-666 on endosome motility.

claim: In wild-type cells, Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles associated with actin cables for ~4.6 s.
source: Here we show that in this step, Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles in wild-type cells associated with actin cables for ~4.6 s and moved on cables about 0.4 μm after internalization (Figure 4A,B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A,B,C.

claim: In wild-type cells, Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles moved on cables about 0.4 μm after internalization.
source: Here we show that in this step, Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles in wild-type cells associated with actin cables for ~4.6 s and moved on cables about 0.4 μm after internalization (Figure 4A,B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4A,B,C.

claim: Association and movements of Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles with actin cables were significantly decreased by treating with 25 μM SMIFH2.
source: This association and these movements were significantly decreased by treating with 25 μM SMIFH2 (Figure 4B,C,D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B,C,D.

claim: Over 80% of Pan1-mCherry-labeled endocytic vesicles associated with and internalized along actin cables in the pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Over 80% of Pan1-mCherry-labeled endocytic vesicles, even in single focal plane images, also associated with and internalized along actin cables in the pan1-18TA mutant (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Pan1-18TA-mCherry structures became stably associated with peripheral patches, as well as actin clumps.
source: In contrast to wild-type cells, Pan1-18TA-mCherry structures became stably associated with peripheral patches, as well as actin clumps, labeled by Abp140-3GFP (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Many internalized patches labeled by Pan1-18TA-mCherry stably associated with actin cables over 30 s.
source: Interestingly, live-cell imaging revealed that many of internalized patches labeled by Pan1-18TA-mCherry stably associated with actin cables over 30 s, and move on actin cables more than 3.0 μm (Figure 4B,C,E, and Video 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B,C,E and Video 4.

claim: Internalized patches labeled by Pan1-18TA-mCherry move on actin cables more than 3.0 μm.
source: Interestingly, live-cell imaging revealed that many of internalized patches labeled by Pan1-18TA-mCherry stably associated with actin cables over 30 s, and move on actin cables more than 3.0 μm (Figure 4B,C,E, and Video 4).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B,C,E and Video 4.

claim: In the pan1-18TA mutant, peripheral Pan1-18TA-mCherry patches colocalized and moved together with Hse1p-labeled endosomes.
source: In the pan1-18TA mutant, we often observed that peripheral Pan1-18TA-mCherry patches colocalized and moved together with Hse1p-labeled endosomes (Figure 4F,G, and Video 5), whereas such colocalization was rarely observed in wild-type cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4F,G and Video 5.

claim: Colocalization of Pan1-mCherry patches with Hse1p-labeled endosomes was rarely observed in wild-type cells.
source: In the pan1-18TA mutant, we often observed that peripheral Pan1-18TA-mCherry patches colocalized and moved together with Hse1p-labeled endosomes (Figure 4F,G, and Video 5), whereas such colocalization was rarely observed in wild-type cells (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In the pan1-18TA mutant, endocytic vesicles and endosomes interact before fusion while they are both associated with actin cables, potentially tethering them together.
source: These findings suggest that in the pan1-18TA mutant, endocytic vesicles and endosomes interact before fusion while they are both associated with actin cables, potentially tethering them together.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the colocalization and co-movement data.

claim: At 1 min after treatment of ark1△ prk1-as3 mutant with 100 μM 1NA-PP1, endocytic vesicles stably associated with, and moved on actin cables.
source: However, at 1 min after treatment of the mutant with 100 μM 1NA-PP1, endocytic vesicles stably associated with, and moved on actin cables.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A and Video 6.

claim: By 3 min after 1NA-PP1 treatment, small aggregates containing Pan1p that associated with actin cables were formed in ark1△ prk1-as3 mutant.
source: By 3 min small aggregates containing Pan1p that associated with actin cables were formed (Figure 5A and Video 6).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A and Video 6.

claim: At 10 min after 1NA-PP1 treatment, a large actin clump that stably associated with actin cables was formed in ark1△ prk1-as3 mutant.
source: At 10 min after 1NA-PP1 treatment, a large actin clump that stably associated with actin cables was formed in the mutant, similar to the pan1-18TA mutant (Figure 5A and Video 6; also see Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5A and Video 6.

claim: Pan1p phosphorylation by Ark1/Prk1 kinases is necessary for the rapid dissociation of endocytic vesicles from actin cables.
source: These observations support the idea that Pan1p phosphorylation by Ark1/Prk1 kinases is necessary for the rapid dissociation of endocytic vesicles from actin cables.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the 1NA-PP1 treatment experiments.

claim: Pan1p can bind directly to F-actin.
source: Pan1p can bind directly to F-actin and its binding activity is regulated by phosphorylation through the Ark1/Prk1 kinases (Toshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Pan1p's F-actin binding activity is regulated by phosphorylation through the Ark1/Prk1 kinases.
source: Pan1p can bind directly to F-actin and its binding activity is regulated by phosphorylation through the Ark1/Prk1 kinases (Toshima et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Combining the pan1-18TA and pan1△855–1480 mutations (pan1-18TA△855) caused accumulation of Pan1-mCherry vesicles similar to pan1-18TA mutant, but formation of actin clumps were significantly suppressed.
source: Interestingly, combining the pan1-18TA and pan1△855–1480 mutations (pan1-18TA△855) caused accumulation of Pan1-mCherry vesicles similar to pan1-18TA mutant, but formation of actin clumps were significantly suppressed (Figure 5B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 5B,C.

claim: The interaction between Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles and actin cables decreased in pan1-18TA△855, but the vesicles still had an ability to bind actin cables.
source: The interaction between Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles and actin cables also decreased, but the vesicles still had an ability to bind actin cables (Figure 4D), suggesting the existence of additional actin-binding coat protein(s) that stabilize the association of vesicles with actin cables.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There exist additional actin-binding coat protein(s) that stabilize the association of vesicles with actin cables.
source: The interaction between Pan1-mCherry-labeled vesicles and actin cables also decreased, but the vesicles still had an ability to bind actin cables (Figure 4D), suggesting the existence of additional actin-binding coat protein(s) that stabilize the association of vesicles with actin cables.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the residual actin cable binding in pan1-18TA△855.

claim: Deletion of Sla2p in the pan1-18TA mutant decreased the fraction of cells containing actin clumps by 95%.
source: Deletion of Sla2p, a yeast Hip1R-related protein, in the pan1-18TA mutant decreased the fraction of cells containing actin clumps by 95% as detected by Abp1-mCherry in maximum-intensity projections of Z stacks (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Deletion of both Myo3p and Myo5p led to an 85% reduction in actin clump formation in the pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Deletion of both of the yeast type I myosins, Myo3p and Myo5p, led to an 85% reduction and deletion of Sac6p, the yeast homologue of the actin filament bundling protein fimbrin, almost completely suppressed actin clump formation in the pan1-18TA mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Deletion of Sac6p almost completely suppressed actin clump formation in the pan1-18TA mutant.
source: Deletion of both of the yeast type I myosins, Myo3p and Myo5p, led to an 85% reduction and deletion of Sac6p, the yeast homologue of the actin filament bundling protein fimbrin, almost completely suppressed actin clump formation in the pan1-18TA mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Hse1p-labeled endosomes showed a change in localization to the cell periphery in pan1-18TA sla2△, pan1-18TA myo3△5△, and pan1-18TA sac6△ mutants.
source: Interestingly, Hse1p-labeled endosomes showed a change in localization to the cell periphery in all three suppressing mutants (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6B,C.

claim: Pan1-18TA patches accumulate near Hse1p-labeled endosomes at the cell periphery in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells.
source: We also observed that Pan1-18TA patches accumulate near Hse1p-labeled endosomes at the cell periphery in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Around half of the endocytic vesicles were able to internalize in sac6△ cells.
source: As reported previously (Gheorghe et al., 2008), deletion of the SAC6 gene increased the lifetime of actin patches, but around half of the endocytic vesicles were able to internalize (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D), indicating that the formation of endocytic vesicles is delayed but eventually occurred.
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: In pan1-18TA sac6△ cells, ~5.3% of patches were still internalized.
source: In contrast, in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells, the lifetime of actin patches were significantly increased and their internalizations were markedly decreased, but ~5.3% of patches were still internalized (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Many vesicle-like structures (~40–60 nm) accumulate around the cell periphery in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells.
source: Interestingly, we observed many vesicle-like structures (~40–60 nm) accumulating around the cell periphery in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells, whereas in wild-type cells such structures were rarely detected (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–C.

claim: Several endosome-like structures (~200–300 nm) associate with vesicle-like structures in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells.
source: We also observed that several endosome-like structures (~200–300 nm) associate with these vesicles in this mutant (Figure 6—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Endosome-like structures associate with ~1–3 small vesicles in two-dimensional cross sections in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells.
source: Quantification of these structures revealed that endosome-like structures associate with ~1–3 small vesicles in two-dimensional cross sections (Figure 6—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Peripheral endosomes in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells are less motile (~17.8 nm/s), compared to prevacuolar ones (~189.0 nm/s).
source: Examining Hse1-GFP in overlaid time-lapse images of pan1-18TA sac6△ cells demonstrated its localization exclusively at the cell periphery and vacuolar membrane, and that peripheral endosomes are less motile (~17.8 nm/s), compared to prevacuolar ones (~189.0 nm/s) (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6E,F.

claim: The peripheral immotile endosomes observed in pan1-18TA sac6△ mutant are likely early endosomes.
source: Since the pan1-18TA sac6△ double mutant has apparently normal late endosomes at the vacuolar membrane, similar to wild-type cells (Figure 6E), the peripheral immotile endosomes observed in the mutant are likely early endosomes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization and motility data.

claim: Peripheral endosomes were rarely observed in the sac6△ mutant.
source: Such peripheral endosomes were rarely observed in the sac6△ mutant (Figure 6E), suggesting that they are due to the mutation of the phosphorylation sites in Pan1p and not just due to the defects in the actin cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: LatA treatment had no effect on endosome localization in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells.
source: LatA treatment had no effect on endosome localization in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells (Figure 6G), supporting the contention that endocytic vesicles and early endosomes stably associate, independently of actin.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Endocytic vesicles and early endosomes stably associate, independently of actin.
source: LatA treatment had no effect on endosome localization in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells (Figure 6G), supporting the contention that endocytic vesicles and early endosomes stably associate, independently of actin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the LatA treatment data in pan1-18TA sac6△ cells.

claim: Pan1p is one of the key regulators that fixes vesicles to the actin cable and then dissociate from the cable and the vesicle upon phosphorylation.
source: Thus, Pan1p seems to be one of the key regulators that fixes vesicles to the actin cable and then dissociate from the cable and the vesicle upon phosphorylation (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data and shown in the model in Figure 7.

claim: After phosphorylation of Pan1p by Ark1/Prk1 kinases, the endocytic vesicle is uncoated, making it possible to fuse to the early endosome.
source: After phosphorylation of Pan1p by Ark1/Prk1 kinases, the endocytic vesicle is uncoated, making it possible to fuse to the early endosome.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The cycle of Pan1 phosphorylation could release endocytic vesicles from the actin cable precisely at the time of their fusion to the endosome.
source: Thus the cycle of Pan1 phosphorylation could release endocytic vesicles from the actin cable precisely at the time of their fusion to the endosome, also allowing the endosome which is indirectly tethered to then move on and mature into a late endosome.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Cargo transport from early to late endosomes is achieved by endosome maturation, which is a successive and rapid process accompanied by Rab5-Rab7 conversion.
source: Many lines of evidence indicate that cargo transport from early to late endosomes is achieved by endosome maturation, which is a successive and rapid process accompanied by Rab5-Rab7 conversion (Balderhaar and Ungermann, 2013; Nordmann et al., 2010; Poteryaev et al., 2010; Rink et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Vps21p is localized not only at early, but also at late endosomes.
source: Since Vps21p is localized not only at early, but also at late endosomes (Toshima et al., 2014), it is difficult to determine the point at which the early endosome ends and the late endosome begins.
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: Recruitment of early ESCRT components to the endosome occurs at a relatively early stage.
source: For instance, subunits of the ESCRT-0, I, and II complex are highly localized but the subunit of ESCRT-III or Vps4p is localized only partially at actin clumps in the pan1-18TA mutant, suggesting that recruitment of early ESCRT components to the endosome occurs at a relatively early stage (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential localization of ESCRT components to actin clumps.

claim: Vps21p is recruited to the endosomal membrane after the start of ESCRT complex formation.
source: Yet Vps21p exhibited only partial localization at actin clumps, suggesting that Vps21p is recruited to the endosomal membrane after the start of ESCRT complex formation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization data.

claim: The retromer complex mediates retrograde transport to the Golgi at the late endosome stage.
source: Vps26p, a component of the retromer complex, is rarely localized at actin clumps and is predominantly localized at the vacuolar membrane, suggesting that the retromer complex mediates retrograde transport to the Golgi at the late endosome stage (Figure 7).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the localization data.

claim: Dissociation of early endosomes from the actin filaments might be a trigger for the initiation of endosome maturation.
source: We demonstrated that early endosomes associate with actin filaments and then change their localization to the vacuolar membrane. This suggests that dissociation of early endosomes from the actin filaments might be a trigger for the initiation of endosome maturation.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Before endosomes move from the plasma membrane to the lysosome along microtubules in mammalian cells, endosomes associate with the cortical actin cytoskeleton underlying the plasma membrane.
source: In mammalian cells, before endosomes move from the plasma membrane to the lysosome along microtubules, endosomes associate with the cortical actin cytoskeleton underlying the plasma membrane (Aschenbrenner et al., 2004; Fernandez-Borja et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: The interaction between endosomes and actin in mammalian cells is regulated by RhoB GTPase.
source: The interaction between endosomes and actin is regulated by RhoB GTPase, an upstream recruiter and activator of mammalian Dia1 and PRK1/PKN (Fernandez-Borja et al., 2005; Mellor et al., 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citations to prior work.

claim: Expression of activated RhoB facilitates the association of early endosomes with cortical actin filaments in mammalian cells.
source: Expression of activated RhoB facilitates the association of early endosomes with cortical actin filaments, which prevents the transfer of endosomes to microtubules and inhibits further transport (Fernandez-Borja et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text with citation to prior work.

claim: The interaction between endosomes and the actin cytoskeleton in mammalian cells might enable endosomes to fuse with endocytic vesicles more efficiently.
source: The physiological importance of the interaction between endosomes and the actin cytoskeleton in mammalian cells has not been determined, but in analogy to our findings this might enable endosomes to fuse with endocytic vesicles more efficiently, at the same time preventing the progression of immature early endosomes to late endosomes.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion drawn by analogy to the yeast findings.
